stacktrace.title: Error Explained
stacktrace.cause: The fetch resolved before the component re-rendered, and results was undefined on the first render pass.
stacktrace.fix: Add a loading guard: `if (!data?.results) return <Spinner />;` before the .map() call. Or initialize with `results: []` in useStarData so the first render is always safe.
stacktrace.footer: Pattern: always guard array operations against undefined before mapping.

codewalk.title: Algorithm Walkthrough

steps.title: Set up the search window
steps.explanation: Start with the full array, lo points to the first element, hi to the last.

steps.title: Pick the midpoint
steps.explanation: Calculate the middle index. The `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` form avoids integer overflow that `(lo + hi) / 2` can cause.

steps.title: Compare and narrow
steps.explanation: If we found it, return. Otherwise, discard the half that cannot contain target. Each step halves the search space, O(log n).

steps.title: Repeat until found or empty
steps.code:
while (lo <= hi) { /* step 2 & 3 */ }
return -1; // not found
steps.explanation: Keep looping while the window has elements. If lo passes hi, the target is not in the array.

codewalk.footer: Binary search: O(log n) time, O(1) space. Requires a sorted array.

queryplan.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE — the bottleneck
queryplan.sql:
SELECT w.*, count(e.id)
FROM widgets w
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.widget_id = w.id
WHERE w.org_id = $1
GROUP BY w.id
queryplan.caption: A sequential scan over 1.24M events — there is no index on events.widget_id.

sequencealign.title: The LCS problem, on real reads
sequencealign.footer: Read 1 carries a single-base substitution (C→A); Read 2 has a 2-base deletion right where Read 1 still matches the reference. The two reads disagree with each other there, so the consensus can't call a base at that column — everywhere else, all three agree.
